verdict.summary: Gorgias says OAuth2 is mandatory for any third-party app, and apps are created as drafts in its partner portal; the in-product connect button only appears after the tech partnership team reviews and approves the app. Getting a sandbox also needs a manual step (a draft app, then an email to techpartners@gorgias.com), and no review timeline is published.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Registering and creating a draft app is quick, but a sandbox account requires emailing techpartners@gorgias.com to convert a trial (new sandboxes start as Demo accounts). The turnaround for that email isn't stated.

timeToProd.assumes: A public OAuth2 app listed in the Gorgias App Store that reads and writes tickets and customers for merchants; there's no documented unlisted path for third parties.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Gorgias tech partnership team review of the submitted app (no SLA published), plus any requested scope changes.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Gorgias publishes no review duration; the range is our estimate.

prerequisites.why: Draft apps, OAuth credentials and the review submission all live in the partner portal.
You test installs on a sandbox subdomain. You need a draft app before Gorgias will convert a trial into a sandbox.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: New sandboxes start as Demo accounts; email techpartners@gorgias.com with the account URL to switch to a Developer plan.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS redirect URL and server-side secret storage
prerequisites.why: The token exchange authenticates with client_id and client_secret, and redirect_uri must match between steps.

prerequisites.item: A test account for your own product
prerequisites.why: The submission has to include testing instructions with a test account.

scopeTiers.tier: Private use with API keys (your own helpdesk)
scopeTiers.impact: Works for a merchant's own internal scripts. Gorgias says OAuth2 is mandatory for third-party apps, so this isn't a route for serving other merchants.
Enough for an agent that triages or summarizes tickets. Requires review like any public app.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Gorgias doesn't say scopes change review time; it says it will ask you to trim scopes your use case doesn't need.

scopeTiers.impact: Needed to reply to or update tickets. Reviewers check scopes against the use case.
Change helpdesk configuration. Expect pushback unless clearly needed (for example installing widgets or webhooks on setup).
A temporary permission that Gorgias says will be removed; use granular scopes instead.

steps.title: Register on the Developer Portal
steps.detail: Sign up as a partner on the Gorgias Developer Portal.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: partners.gorgias.com/signup returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20. We did not sign up.

steps.title: Create a draft app
steps.detail: Create a draft app in the portal with the app name, redirect URL and requested scopes; copy the client_id and client_secret.

steps.title: Create a trial and request a sandbox
steps.detail: Create a Gorgias trial at gorgias.com/signup, then email techpartners@gorgias.com with the account URL to convert it to a Developer plan sandbox.

steps.title: Wait for sandbox conversion
steps.detail: Gorgias converts the account manually; they say they're working on automating it.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth2 flow
steps.detail: Ask the merchant for their Gorgias subdomain. Redirect to https://{subdomain}.gorgias.com/oauth/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope (include offline for a refresh token), state and nonce. Exchange the code at https://{subdomain}.gorgias.com/oauth/token with Basic auth client_id:client_secret.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: That offline is what yields a refresh token is our inference; the docs show it in the granted scope string without explaining it.

steps.title: Implement refresh and reinstall handling
steps.detail: Refresh 24-hour access tokens with grant_type=refresh_token. If the merchant deactivates the app, rerun the full authorization flow.

steps.title: Add one-click setup on install
steps.detail: On install, create the widgets, macros, tags and webhook subscriptions the app needs, so customers don't configure HTTP integrations by hand.

steps.title: Test on the sandbox
steps.detail: Install via the test URL https://{sandbox}.gorgias.com/app/settings/integrations/app/{client_id} and from your own product.

steps.title: Complete the listing and testing instructions
steps.detail: Fill every field in the draft app form, write listing copy and testing instructions with a test account, and justify each scope.

steps.title: Add screenshots and submit
steps.detail: Upload screenshots (they appear on the listing) and submit the app for review in the portal.

steps.title: Tech partnership review
steps.detail: Gorgias checks the app works and matches their expectations, then contacts you with the result or the fixes needed. Approved apps appear in the in-product and public App Store.

agentCanDo: Implement the subdomain-aware OAuth2 flow with state and nonce
Build token refresh and reinstall detection
Pick granular scopes and avoid write:all
Script widget, macro and webhook setup on install
Draft listing copy, testing instructions and scope justifications
Handle 429s with Retry-After and the call-limit header
humanMustDo: Register on the Developer Portal and create the draft app
Create a trial and email techpartners@gorgias.com for a sandbox
Provide a test account and screenshots
Submit for review and respond to feedback
Customer side: a merchant installs from the App Store or your product

blockers.symptom: The Connect button doesn't appear in the merchant's App Store
blockers.cause: The connect button only appears after the app is approved.
blockers.fix: Test via the sandbox test-install URL until approval, then submit for review.

blockers.symptom: Gorgias won't convert your trial to a sandbox
blockers.cause: You need a draft app in the portal before the sandbox can be approved.
blockers.fix: Create the draft app first, then email techpartners@gorgias.com with the account URL.

blockers.symptom: Sandbox behaves like a demo account
blockers.cause: New sandbox accounts are Demo accounts by default.
blockers.fix: Email techpartners@gorgias.com with your account URL to switch it to a Developer plan.

blockers.symptom: Reviewers ask you to change scopes
blockers.cause: The app requests data that isn't needed for its use case.
blockers.fix: Request only the granular scopes you use and explain each.

blockers.cause: OAuth2 apps get 80 requests per 20-second window per account (10-second window on Enterprise accounts).
blockers.fix: Read X-Gorgias-Account-Api-Call-Limit, wait Retry-after seconds, and plan for high-volume merchants during peaks like BFCM.

blockers.symptom: Tokens stop working after the merchant deactivates the app
blockers.cause: Deactivation on the helpdesk requires the full authorization flow again.
blockers.fix: Detect auth failures and prompt the merchant to reconnect.

nuances.text: Access tokens expire after 24 hours (expires_in 86400); refresh tokens have no expiration time.
OAuth2 apps get double the API-key rate limit (80 vs 40 requests per 20 seconds per account), and Enterprise accounts use a tighter 10-second window.
OAuth endpoints are per merchant subdomain, so your connect flow needs the merchant's Gorgias subdomain.
Customers see which data an app can access and can revoke it by disconnecting the app in their settings.
Gorgias's OAuth uses OpenID scopes (openid, email, profile) and supports a nonce, but no OIDC discovery document was found at the account subdomain.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: GET https://acme.gorgias.com/.well-known/openid-configuration returned 404; acme may not be a real account, so this isn't conclusive.

nuances.text: Approved apps are announced at Gorgias's next Product Town Hall, and the Partnerships team offers further promotion.
